title: The Runner I Cheered for
scene: At a local five-kilometer race, a spectator mistakes a runner in a red cap for his friend Leo and cheers wildly. When Leo arrives a minute later, the mistake becomes a joke—and the stranger may have enjoyed the encouragement.
sceneJa: 地域の5キロレースで友人レオを応援。赤い帽子の走者をレオだと思い込み、大声で声援を送った。本人は1分後に登場。間違えた相手も喜んでいたらしく、友人と笑い合う。

chunks.en: I went to cheer for Leo
chunks.ja: レオを応援しに行った

chunks.en: where half the runners seemed to be wearing red caps.
chunks.ja: 走者の半分くらいが赤い帽子をかぶっているように見えた

chunks.en: When a runner in a red cap came around the corner,
chunks.ja: 赤い帽子の走者が角を曲がって現れたとき
その走者があまりに元気よく手を振り返してくれたので
僕はさらに大声で応援した
本物のレオが走ってきて

chunks.en: and asked, 'Who were you cheering for?'
chunks.ja: 「さっき誰を応援してたの？」と聞いた

chunks.en: I couldn't tell you two apart from that distance,'
chunks.ja: あの距離じゃ2人を見分けられなかったんだ」と

chunks.en: I said, still holding my sign.
chunks.ja: 僕は応援ボードを持ったまま言った

chunks.en: that guy looked thrilled,' Leo said,
chunks.ja: あの人、すごく喜んでたよ」とレオは言い

chunks.en: 'so I think you made his day.'
chunks.ja: 「きっといい一日になったんじゃない？」と続けた

questions.question: Which version keeps the natural meaning chunk intact?
options: I got carried away / and shouted Leo's name.
I got / carried away and / shouted Leo's name.
I got carried / away and shouted / Leo's name.
questions.explanation: 'I got carried away' is one natural unit meaning I became overly excited or involved. Pause after it before the next action.

questions.question: What does 'In my defense' mean in this story?
options: The speaker is accusing Leo of cheating.
The speaker is playfully offering an excuse for the mistake.
The speaker is asking the runner to defend him.
questions.explanation: 'In my defense' introduces a reason that might excuse your behavior. Here it is a lighthearted justification, not a legal defense.

questions.question: Why does Leo say the stranger may have had his day made?
options: He thinks the stranger won the race.
He wants the speaker to stop attending races.
He thinks the mistaken cheering made the stranger happy.
questions.explanation: Leo turns an embarrassing mistake into a kind interpretation: unexpected support may have cheered the stranger up.

speak: Imagine: you cheer for a friend at a race and mistake another runner for them. Read: notice the excitement turning into gentle embarrassment. Chunk: say 'I got carried away', 'In my defense', and 'I couldn't tell them apart' as complete units. Understand: the first admits overexcitement, the second introduces a playful excuse, and the third explains a visual mistake. Check: answer all three questions. Speak (30 seconds): describe a time you mixed up two people or objects, explain how you got carried away, and offer a lighthearted excuse. Final Read: read all six sentences without Japanese, pausing after 'In my defense' and softening the final line.
review: New: 'I got carried away'（つい夢中になった）, 'In my defense'（言い訳させてもらうと）, 'I couldn't tell them apart'（見分けられなかった）. Reuse Lesson 102/105 'For what it's worth'（それはそれとして／参考までに）to make a generous comment after a spectator's mistake. Compared with Lessons 94–107, this is a spectator's mistaken identity and playful self-defense, not a shogi trap, meal, invitation, or planning dispute. Reference: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/get-carried-away ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/tell-apart ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/defense .
